CIRCUIT: a 4-column passive ladder (columns B,C,D,E) hung between three horizontal rails, driven by a left-hand vertical branch carrying V-AC#6 (8V 1kHz) above and I-DC#11 (3A) below. Geometry: left vertical x~135; column B x~394; column C x~545 (top) / 540 (middle) / 556 (bottom); column D x~750; column E x~885; right drop x~985. Top rail y~285 (5uH#0 at x~251, 15uF#1 at x~672); middle rail y~470-500 (9uF#7 at x~462, 4uH#8 at x~810); bottom rail y~690 (1uF#16 at x~276, 1uH#17 at x~629). Each column carries an upper diode/zener from the top rail to the middle rail and a lower diode/zener from the middle rail to the bottom rail. The middle rail runs off the right-hand end down through 2k#13 to GND#18; its left-hand end runs off to GND#9 (a ground symbol drawn rotated 90deg at x~48, bars vertical, lead leaving to the right).

JUDGEMENT CALLS - the four degree-4 crossings, all called JUNCTION.
  The decisive global fact: this sheet contains NO hop and NO jog anywhere. I read the whole drawing at 2x (x 0-600 and x 500-1100, y 180-780) looking specifically for semicircular detours or sideways offsets and there are none; every wire-on-wire meeting on the sheet is either a plain T or a plain X. Per the dataset ink prior (drafters draw a hop or a jog when they mean 'not connected'), a sheet with no hop idiom has no intended crossings. All four plain X's therefore read as junctions.
  S17 (134,498) - left vertical (V-AC bottom to I-DC top) x middle rail (GND#9 to column B). inkmap 20px: vertical is a clean 2-3px column at x=132-134 running unbroken y=478..518; the horizontal enters at rows 498-500 on the left and leaves at rows 496-498 on the right, a 2px level difference that is ordinary hand wobble, not a jog. No widening at the meeting point - dot score 1.5 against a 1.1 noise floor, i.e. nothing. (The tracer reported hop=5.7 here; that score is spurious - there is no arc in the pixels.) Chosen reading: junction, so GND#9 grounds the midpoint of the source stack. Other reading (crossing): GND + rail + column B stay together but V-AC bottom / I-DC top become a private 2-terminal net, giving 10 nets and a circuit in which neither source is referenced to ground. Not electrically impossible, but no hop is drawn and it would leave the ground symbol doing nothing useful.
  S11 (540,472) - column C x middle rail. inkmap 20px: vertical 2-3px, unbroken y=452..492; horizontal continuous x=520..560 through it. There is an ink pool at x=529-541, y=470-475, about 12px wide but only 5px tall - asymmetric, so a stroke overlap / pen lead-in, not a solder dot (a dot would be ~9px in BOTH axes here). dot=1.6. Chosen reading: junction, so column C's mid node is the rail. Other reading (crossing): diode#4 bottom + zener#10 top become a private 2-terminal net and n4 loses two terminals; 10 nets.
  S8 (746,468) - column D x middle rail. inkmap 20px: plain X, vertical 3px unbroken y=448..488, horizontal 3px unbroken; no blob at the centre (dot=1.6, the same as S11's overlap). The tracer's hop=5.7 here is the 4uH#8 coil 60px to the right being picked up, not a hop at the crossing. Chosen reading: junction. Other reading (crossing): zener#3 bottom + diode#12 top become a private 2-terminal net.
  S9 (881,467) - column E x middle rail. inkmap 20px: plain X, no widening, dot=1.4; hop=2.1 is again the 4uH coil to the left. Chosen reading: junction. Other reading (crossing): diode#5 bottom + diode#14 top become a private 2-terminal net, and 4uH right + 2k top would be a bare 2-terminal net.
  Structural cross-check that supports junction at all four: column B unambiguously joins the middle rail (S12/S13 below are degree-3 T's - the rail physically ends on the column there), so the drafter's middle rail is a tapping rail, not a pass-through. If instead S8/S9/S11/S17 were all crossings, the middle rail would degenerate into a source-free loop GND#9 - 9uF - 4uH - 2k - GND#18 that taps nothing, with all four columns reduced to isolated 2-diode chains. That is a pointless drawing; the junction reading gives the ordinary 4-rung ladder the sheet obviously depicts.

GAP BRIDGE: B0 (761,282)->(756,286) KEPT. inkmap 22px at (757,285) shows the top rail arriving from the 15uF cap and ending at x=758 on rows 284-285, the column-D vertical dropping from (756,286), and the continuation of the top rail restarting at x=761 on rows 280-283 and running on to column E. The 3px diagonal gap is a pen lift in the middle of one straight rail - the right-hand segment has no other possible origin - so the bridge is real and column D's top lead sits on n3. Dropping it would leave zener#3 top on a 1-terminal net and diode#5 top with only the 15uF cap.

CLASSES: all 19 checked against the drawing and all correct. #2, #3 and #10 have the bent (hooked) cathode bar of a Zener; #4, #5, #12, #14, #15 have a straight bar and are plain diodes. #9 is a genuine GND drawn rotated 90 degrees (three bars of decreasing length, lead leaving to the right) - it is easy to mistake for a capacitor at first glance but the third, shortest bar settles it. There are no 3-terminal parts on this sheet, so no pin-order questions. No component is unconnected; no merges were needed.
